mediators.name: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling
mediators.source_query: icariin[Title/Abstract] AND (Wnt[Title/Abstract] OR beta-catenin[Title/Abstract] OR CTNNB1[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (Wnt[Title/Abstract] OR beta-catenin[Title/Abstract] OR CTNNB1[Title/Abstract]) AND osteoblast differentiation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Icariin activates Wnt/beta-catenin pathway; beta-catenin nuclear signaling is a canonical driver of osteoblast commitment and differentiation.

mediators.name: BMP2
mediators.source_query: icariin[Title/Abstract] AND (BMP2[Title/Abstract] OR bone morphogenetic protein 2[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (BMP2[Title/Abstract] OR bone morphogenetic protein 2[Title/Abstract]) AND osteoblast differentiation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Icariin upregulates BMP2 expression; BMP2 is a master regulator of osteoblast differentiation via SMAD signaling.

mediators.name: Runx2
mediators.source_query: icariin[Title/Abstract] AND (Runx2[Title/Abstract] OR RUNX2[Title/Abstract] OR Cbfa1[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (Runx2[Title/Abstract] OR RUNX2[Title/Abstract] OR Cbfa1[Title/Abstract]) AND osteoblast differentiation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Icariin modulates Runx2 transcription factor levels; Runx2 is the primary transcriptional determinant of osteoblast lineage specification.

mediators.name: Bcl-2
mediators.source_query: curcumin[Title/Abstract] AND (Bcl-2[Title/Abstract] OR BCL2[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (Bcl-2[Title/Abstract] OR BCL2[Title/Abstract]) AND apoptosis[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Curcumin downregulates anti-apoptotic Bcl-2; reduced Bcl-2 releases cytochrome c and activates caspase-dependent apoptosis in cancer cells.

mediators.name: NF-kappaB
mediators.source_query: curcumin[Title/Abstract] AND (NF-kappaB[Title/Abstract] OR NF-kB[Title/Abstract] OR nuclear factor kappa B[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (NF-kappaB[Title/Abstract] OR NF-kB[Title/Abstract] OR nuclear factor kappa B[Title/Abstract]) AND apoptosis[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Curcumin inhibits NF-kappaB activation; NF-kappaB suppression removes survival signals and sensitizes tumor cells to apoptotic stimuli.

mediators.name: p53
mediators.source_query: curcumin[Title/Abstract] AND (p53[Title/Abstract] OR TP53[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (p53[Title/Abstract] OR TP53[Title/Abstract]) AND apoptosis[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Curcumin stabilizes and activates p53; p53 transcriptionally induces pro-apoptotic genes including PUMA and BAX to execute apoptosis.

mediators.name: dysbiosis
mediators.source_query: CFTR[Title/Abstract] AND (dysbiosis[Title/Abstract] OR gut microbiome[Title/Abstract] OR intestinal microbiota[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (dysbiosis[Title/Abstract] OR gut microbiome[Title/Abstract] OR intestinal microbiota[Title/Abstract]) AND intestinal inflammation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: CFTR dysfunction alters intestinal pH and mucus, driving microbiome dysbiosis; dysbiotic communities promote mucosal immune activation and intestinal inflammation.

mediators.name: IL-8
mediators.source_query: CFTR[Title/Abstract] AND (IL-8[Title/Abstract] OR interleukin-8[Title/Abstract] OR CXCL8[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (IL-8[Title/Abstract] OR interleukin-8[Title/Abstract] OR CXCL8[Title/Abstract]) AND intestinal inflammation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: CFTR-deficient epithelial cells constitutively overproduce IL-8; IL-8 recruits neutrophils to the intestinal mucosa, amplifying inflammatory tissue damage.

mediators.name: ER stress
mediators.source_query: CFTR[Title/Abstract] AND (ER stress[Title/Abstract] OR endoplasmic reticulum stress[Title/Abstract] OR unfolded protein response[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (ER stress[Title/Abstract] OR endoplasmic reticulum stress[Title/Abstract] OR unfolded protein response[Title/Abstract]) AND intestinal inflammation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Misfolded CFTR accumulates in ER, triggering UPR/ER stress; ER stress in intestinal epithelium activates inflammatory NF-kappaB and MAPK cascades.

mediators.name: oxidative stress
mediators.source_query: SMN[Title/Abstract] AND (oxidative stress[Title/Abstract] OR reactive oxygen species[Title/Abstract] OR ROS[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (oxidative stress[Title/Abstract] OR reactive oxygen species[Title/Abstract] OR ROS[Title/Abstract]) AND mitochondrial dysfunction[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: SMN-deficient motor neurons exhibit elevated ROS; oxidative stress damages mitochondrial membranes and respiratory chain complexes, causing mitochondrial dysfunction.

mediators.name: Plastin 3
mediators.source_query: SMN[Title/Abstract] AND (Plastin 3[Title/Abstract] OR PLS3[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (Plastin 3[Title/Abstract] OR PLS3[Title/Abstract]) AND mitochondrial dysfunction[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: PLS3 modifies SMA severity downstream of SMN; PLS3 interacts with actin dynamics affecting mitochondrial trafficking and function in neurons.

mediators.name: autophagy
mediators.source_query: SMN[Title/Abstract] AND (autophagy[Title/Abstract] OR mitophagy[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (autophagy[Title/Abstract] OR mitophagy[Title/Abstract]) AND mitochondrial dysfunction[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: SMN deficiency impairs autophagic flux; defective mitophagy allows accumulation of damaged mitochondria, perpetuating mitochondrial dysfunction in motor neurons.

mediators.name: regulatory T cells
mediators.source_query: PD-1 blockade[Title/Abstract] AND (regulatory T cell[Title/Abstract] OR Treg[Title/Abstract] OR FOXP3[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (regulatory T cell[Title/Abstract] OR Treg[Title/Abstract] OR FOXP3[Title/Abstract]) AND immune-related adverse event[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: PD-1 blockade depletes or impairs Tregs; reduced Treg suppression allows autoreactive T cells to attack normal tissues, precipitating immune-related adverse events.

mediators.name: IL-17
mediators.source_query: PD-1 blockade[Title/Abstract] AND (IL-17[Title/Abstract] OR interleukin-17[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (IL-17[Title/Abstract] OR interleukin-17[Title/Abstract]) AND immune-related adverse event[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: PD-1 inhibition expands Th17 cells elevating IL-17; IL-17-driven neutrophilic inflammation underlies colitis and pneumonitis irAEs.

mediators.name: CTLA-4
mediators.source_query: PD-1 blockade[Title/Abstract] AND (CTLA-4[Title/Abstract] OR CTLA4[Title/Abstract] OR CD152[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (CTLA-4[Title/Abstract] OR CTLA4[Title/Abstract] OR CD152[Title/Abstract]) AND immune-related adverse event[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: PD-1 blockade upregulates compensatory CTLA-4 expression; residual CTLA-4 pathway perturbation modulates irAE spectrum and severity independently.

mediators.name: NF-kappaB
mediators.source_query: dystrophin deficiency[Title/Abstract] AND (NF-kappaB[Title/Abstract] OR NF-kB[Title/Abstract] OR nuclear factor kappa B[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (NF-kappaB[Title/Abstract] OR NF-kB[Title/Abstract] OR nuclear factor kappa B[Title/Abstract]) AND chronic inflammation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Membrane fragility in dystrophin-deficient muscle constitutively activates NF-kappaB; sustained NF-kappaB drives cytokine production maintaining chronic muscle inflammation.

mediators.name: NLRP3 inflammasome
mediators.source_query: dystrophin deficiency[Title/Abstract] AND (NLRP3[Title/Abstract] OR inflammasome[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (NLRP3[Title/Abstract] OR inflammasome[Title/Abstract]) AND chronic inflammation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Calcium influx and mitochondrial damage in dystrophin-null fibers activate NLRP3 inflammasome; NLRP3-driven IL-1beta release sustains chronic inflammatory cycles.

mediators.name: macrophage polarization
mediators.source_query: dystrophin deficiency[Title/Abstract] AND (macrophage polarization[Title/Abstract] OR M1 macrophage[Title/Abstract] OR macrophage infiltration[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (macrophage polarization[Title/Abstract] OR M1 macrophage[Title/Abstract] OR pro-inflammatory macrophage[Title/Abstract]) AND chronic inflammation[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Necrotic dystrophin-deficient fibers recruit and skew macrophages toward M1 phenotype; persistent M1 macrophage dominance perpetuates chronic inflammatory tissue damage.

mediators.name: SASP
mediators.source_query: endothelial senescence[Title/Abstract] AND (SASP[Title/Abstract] OR senescence-associated secretory phenotype[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (SASP[Title/Abstract] OR senescence-associated secretory phenotype[Title/Abstract]) AND atherosclerosis[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Senescent endothelial cells secrete SASP factors; SASP cytokines recruit monocytes and promote foam cell formation, accelerating atherosclerotic plaque development.

mediators.name: p16INK4a
mediators.source_query: endothelial senescence[Title/Abstract] AND (p16[Title/Abstract] OR CDKN2A[Title/Abstract] OR p16INK4a[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (p16[Title/Abstract] OR CDKN2A[Title/Abstract] OR p16INK4a[Title/Abstract]) AND atherosclerosis[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: p16INK4a accumulates in senescent endothelium impairing cell cycle; p16-positive senescent cells in plaques correlate with atherosclerotic lesion burden and instability.

mediators.name: eNOS uncoupling
mediators.source_query: endothelial senescence[Title/Abstract] AND (eNOS uncoupling[Title/Abstract] OR eNOS[Title/Abstract] OR endothelial nitric oxide synthase[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (eNOS uncoupling[Title/Abstract] OR eNOS[Title/Abstract] OR endothelial nitric oxide synthase[Title/Abstract]) AND atherosclerosis[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Senescent endothelial cells exhibit eNOS uncoupling reducing NO bioavailability; impaired NO signaling promotes endothelial dysfunction and pro-atherogenic lipid oxidation.

mediators.name: HBx protein
mediators.source_query: hepatitis B virus[Title/Abstract] AND (HBx[Title/Abstract] OR hepatitis B x protein[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (HBx[Title/Abstract] OR hepatitis B x protein[Title/Abstract]) AND hepatocellular carcinoma[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: HBV encodes HBx oncoprotein that transactivates host oncogenes; HBx disrupts p53 function and activates Wnt/beta-catenin, directly driving hepatocellular carcinoma.

mediators.name: DNA methylation
mediators.source_query: hepatitis B virus[Title/Abstract] AND (DNA methylation[Title/Abstract] OR epigenetic silencing[Title/Abstract] OR promoter methylation[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (DNA methylation[Title/Abstract] OR epigenetic silencing[Title/Abstract] OR promoter methylation[Title/Abstract]) AND hepatocellular carcinoma[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Chronic HBV infection induces aberrant DNA methylation silencing tumor suppressors; epigenetic reprogramming of hepatocytes is a non-mutagenic route to hepatocellular carcinoma.

mediators.name: hepatic stellate cell activation
mediators.source_query: hepatitis B virus[Title/Abstract] AND (hepatic stellate cell activation[Title/Abstract] OR HSC activation[Title/Abstract] OR liver fibrosis[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (hepatic stellate cell activation[Title/Abstract] OR HSC activation[Title/Abstract]) AND hepatocellular carcinoma[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: HBV-driven hepatic stellate cell activation creates fibrotic niche; activated HSCs secrete HGF and TGF-beta creating tumor-permissive microenvironment for hepatocellular carcinoma.

mediators.name: tubuloglomerular feedback
mediators.source_query: SGLT2 inhibitor[Title/Abstract] AND (tubuloglomerular feedback[Title/Abstract] OR afferent arteriole[Title/Abstract] OR glomerular hyperfiltration[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (tubuloglomerular feedback[Title/Abstract] OR glomerular hyperfiltration[Title/Abstract]) AND renal protection[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors restore tubuloglomerular feedback by reducing proximal sodium reabsorption; corrected TGF reduces glomerular hyperfiltration, a key renoprotective mechanism.

mediators.name: AMPK
mediators.source_query: SGLT2 inhibitor[Title/Abstract] AND (AMPK[Title/Abstract] OR AMP-activated protein kinase[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (AMPK[Title/Abstract] OR AMP-activated protein kinase[Title/Abstract]) AND renal protection[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: SGLT2 inhibition activates renal AMPK via energy sensing; AMPK suppresses mTORC1 and oxidative stress in tubular cells, conferring direct renoprotection.

mediators.name: ketone bodies
mediators.source_query: SGLT2 inhibitor[Title/Abstract] AND (ketone bodies[Title/Abstract] OR beta-hydroxybutyrate[Title/Abstract] OR BHB[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (ketone bodies[Title/Abstract] OR beta-hydroxybutyrate[Title/Abstract] OR BHB[Title/Abstract]) AND renal protection[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: SGLT2 inhibitors elevate circulating ketone bodies; beta-hydroxybutyrate acts as HDAC inhibitor and NLRP3 suppressor in renal tubular cells, providing renoprotection.

mediators.name: short-chain fatty acids
mediators.source_query: gut dysbiosis[Title/Abstract] AND (short-chain fatty acids[Title/Abstract] OR SCFA[Title/Abstract] OR butyrate[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (short-chain fatty acids[Title/Abstract] OR SCFA[Title/Abstract] OR butyrate[Title/Abstract]) AND bone loss[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Dysbiosis reduces SCFA-producing bacteria; SCFAs regulate osteoclast differentiation via GPR signaling and Treg induction, linking microbiome composition to bone loss.

mediators.name: serotonin
mediators.source_query: gut dysbiosis[Title/Abstract] AND (serotonin[Title/Abstract] OR 5-hydroxytryptamine[Title/Abstract] OR TPH1[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (serotonin[Title/Abstract] OR 5-hydroxytryptamine[Title/Abstract] OR gut-derived serotonin[Title/Abstract]) AND bone loss[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Dysbiosis alters gut-derived serotonin synthesis via TPH1; elevated peripheral serotonin inhibits osteoblast proliferation, providing a non-obvious gut-bone axis mechanism.

mediators.name: intestinal permeability
mediators.source_query: gut dysbiosis[Title/Abstract] AND (intestinal permeability[Title/Abstract] OR leaky gut[Title/Abstract] OR tight junction[Title/Abstract])
mediators.target_query: (intestinal permeability[Title/Abstract] OR leaky gut[Title/Abstract] OR gut barrier[Title/Abstract]) AND bone loss[Title/Abstract]
mediators.rationale: Dysbiosis disrupts tight junctions increasing intestinal permeability; bacterial LPS translocation activates systemic RANKL-mediated osteoclastogenesis driving bone loss.
